And he stayed in the palace for a few days,
and from there he went to Balad.
And Hazarasp the commander entreatied the Sultan concerning Balad that it should not be plundered.
And the Sultan replied:
"Behold, you see that our treasuries are empty,
and those who are with us are hungry and pressuring us,
and there is no recourse except plunder.
Rather, go on this night and bring out the inhabitants of the city, both great and small,
and let them take for themselves whatever they can from their houses."
And when he had done so,
the Ghuzz entered the city and plundered it.
And Hazarasp sent the inhabitants of the city to Mosul;
they were ten thousand men, besides women and children;
and he sent with them someone to protect them on the way.
Now the chiefs of the Ma'addites,
except for al-Basasiri, who had fled to Syria and allied himself with the Egyptians,
when they saw that they could not withstand the force of the Ghuzz,
sent and sued for peace.
And the Sultan received them,
and showed them love,
and clothed them in honorable garments.
And he wished to go to Armenia, to the land of Ibn Marwan.
Then the chiefs of the Ma'addites pleaded with him:
"He too has offended just as we have offended,
and we beseech you that you also forgive him just as you have forgiven us."
The Sultan replied:
"You confessed your folly,
and it was forgiven you;
and if he also confesses,
it shall be forgiven him too."
And the Sultan went to the Island of Qardu (Jazirat Ibn Umar),
and its inhabitants submitted to him,
and gave much gold, and they were not taken captive.
And twenty Ghuzz horsemen went up to the monastery of the Nestorians called of Akhmul (Khamul? {OCR?}):
and there were in it at that time four hundred monks.
And they slaughtered one hundred and twenty monks of them,
and the remainder ransomed their lives with six measures of gold and silver.
Now Ibn Marwan sent envoys to the Sultan,
and humbled himself greatly,
and gave a hundred thousand dinars,
and the Sultan made peace with him.
And he turned back, encamped against Shiyar {OCR?}, and captured it,
and killed four thousand men in it,
until their blood flowed in their streets.
And he burned the great mosque that was in it,
and laid waste all its courts.
And because the air stank from the corpses of the slain,
the Sultan withdrew from it and encamped against Tell A'far.
